summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for worsening dyspnea and cough. Evaluation revealed elevated BNP of 5,376 and bilateral lung crackles, consistent with acute on chronic heart failure. He was treated with IV furosemide and showed symptomatic improvement, with resolution of hypoxemia and weaning off supplemental oxygen. An echocardiogram showed stable moderate pericardial effusion, normal ejection fraction, and increased pulmonary artery pressure. He was transitioned to oral torsemide 100 mg twice daily. His transplant medications were continued with a slight increase in tacrolimus dose. He remained stable, with improved respiratory status, and was discharged home with instructions for weight monitoring, lab follow-up, and outpatient management of fluid status.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
End stage renal disease status post kidney transplant
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
